actual_author_read_scope: Complete main text, methods, results, Tables1–2, discussion and all captions; all four original figures visually inspected.

claims.paraphrase: CnbE is hydratase (279 residues); CnbF is decarboxylase (262 residues). Both are classified as tentative by homology in the abstract and discussion.
The caption additionally reports coupled CnbE/CnbF coexpression activity in recombinant E. coli, with data not shown. This is limited experimental support, not isolated-enzyme characterization.
Named constructs use BL21(DE3), pET21a except CnbH in pET28a. Table1 supplies CnbG but no CnbE/F construct details.
CnbG extract converts unchlorinated 2-hydroxymuconate to a keto product by 296-to236nm spectral shift; empty-vector control is included.
Chlorinated tautomerase scope is named, but Figure3 directly tests the unchlorinated substrate. Do not conflate CnbH deaminase activity with CnbG tautomerase.
Chlorinated compound numbering/names and CnbI mass/length/function descriptions contain inconsistencies; they do not establish exact modern route chemistry.
The paper calls AP3 AmnD the deaminase, conflicting with PMID11081795 abstract D/F assignments. Preserve conflict pending deposit/full primary resolution.
Plasmid curing abolishes nitrobenzene/chloronitrobenzene growth. This does not prove the complete catechol PWY5420 route in CNB1; neighboring catA evidence concerns ortho cleavage.
CnbR regulation is explicitly unresolved; a putative regulator is not a demonstrated causal regulatory edge.
Figure4 labels BAB03536 deaminase as AmnE, while Discussion calls the deaminase AmnD. The paper is internally inconsistent; ENA also labels BAB03536 as AmnE.

limits: No isolated CnbF/CnbE stoichiometry, metal requirement, exact stereochemistry or independent current sequence identity demonstrated.
Gene/frame mapping retains CnbF MONOMER14737/G11246 and CnbE MONOMER14738/G11247 from native objects; publication itself uses gene names.
